name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+13 partisan lean anchors the race for Democrats
Incumbent Grijalva holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 99 percent
No public polling, so the estimate rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: This Tucson-area seat leans 13 points Democratic, incumbent Adelita Grijalva has out-raised Republican Daniel Butierez roughly ten to one, and prediction markets put her odds near 99 percent. Fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin even without any public polling to check against.
model.watch: An unexpectedly harsh national midterm environment or a low-turnout anomaly could narrow the margin, though it would take an extreme shift to put the seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 7th District, anchored in Tucson, carries a 13-point Democratic partisan lean and has been held by Democrats for years. Adelita Grijalva, who won the seat in a 2025 special election, is running for a full term and has raised about $2.3 million, roughly ten times the total of Republican Daniel Butierez, who had under $12,000 in cash late in the cycle. Outside groups have spent modestly to support her with little opposition activity.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Grijalva win at about 99 percent. With no expert ratings flagging the seat as competitive, the forecast calls it safely Democratic, with an expected margin in the low twenties.
